sections.heading: Preface
sections.text: The aim of this book is to provide a readable account of the examples and fundamental results of groups from a theoretical point of view and a geometrical point of view. The concept of a group is one of the most fundamental in modern mathematics. Groups are systems consisting of a set of elements and a binary operation that can be applied to two elements of the set, which together satisfy certain axioms. These require that the group is closed under the operation (the combination of any two elements produces another element of the group), that it obey the associative law, that it contains an identity element (which, combined with any other element, leaves the latter unchanged), and that each element have an inverse (which combines with an element to produce the identity element). Since the book does not make any assumptions about the reader’s background, it is suitable for newcomers to group theory and even those who never studied algebra. To explain many subjects we used figures and images to help the readers. The book is organized into eleven chapters. To get to any depth in group theory requires set theory, combinatorics, number theory, matrixtheory, andgeometry. Thus, not only we have devoted Chaps. 1 – 2 to the introductory concepts of set theory, combinations, number theory, and symmetry, but we have also devoted some parts of Chap. 7 to matrix theory. Although the main subject of the book is groups but in many parts we will need some information about other algebraic structures, like rings, fields and vector spaces. In Chap. 3 , we give the definitions of group and subgroup, examples and some elementary properties. Several excellent and important examples of groups like cyclic groups, permutation groups, group of arithmetical functions, matrixgroupsandlineargroupsareinvestigatedinChaps. 4 – 7 .InChap. 8 ,Lagrange’s theorem as the most important theorem in finite groups is discussed. Chapters 9 – 11 address the normal subgroups, factor groups, derived subgroup, homomorphism, isomorphism and automorphism of groups. A consequence is Cayley’s theorem in which every group could be realized as a permutation group. Some chapters or sections are labelled as optional; this means that the readers can ignore them for the first study. Each section ends in a collection of exercises. The purpose of these exercises is to allow students to test their assimilation of the material, v vi Preface to challenge their knowledge and ability. Moreover, at the end of each chapter we have two special sections: (1) Worked-Out Problems; (2) Supplementary Exercises. In each worked-out problems section, I decided to try teach by examples, by writing out to solutions to problems. In choosing problems, three major criteria have been considered, to be challenging, interesting and educational. Moreover, there are many exercises at the end of each chapter as supplementary exercises. They are harder than before and serve to present the interesting concepts and theorems which are not discussed in the text. The list of references at the end of the book is confined to works actually used in the text. Yazd, Iran Bijan Davvaz

claims.text: A group is a system consisting of a set of elements and a binary operation that can be applied to two elements of the set, which together satisfy certain axioms.
The book provides a readable account of the examples and fundamental results of groups from a theoretical point of view and a geometrical point of view.
Groups are systems consisting of a set of elements and a binary operation that can be applied to two elements of the set, which together satisfy certain axioms.
The concept of a group is one of the most fundamental in modern mathematics.
Permutation groups are a fundamental concept in abstract algebra, and they play a crucial role in various areas of mathematics, including group theory, combinatorics, and geometry.
The symmetric group Sn is the group of all permutations of a set with n elements, and it has n! elements.
The alternating group An is the subgroup of Sn consisting of all even permutations, and it has n!/2 elements.
Permutation groups can be used to study the symmetries of objects, and they have numerous applications in physics, chemistry, and computer science.

concepts.name: Permutation group
concepts.definition: A group of permutations of a set with a given number of elements, with the operation being function composition.

concepts.name: Symmetric group
concepts.definition: The group of all permutations of a set with n elements, denoted as Sn.

concepts.name: Alternating group
concepts.definition: The subgroup of Sn consisting of all even permutations, denoted as An.

claims.text: Arithmetical functions are functions defined on the set of positive integers, and they assign real or complex numbers to these integers.
The Dirichlet product is a binary operation on arithmetical functions, and it is used to define the convolution of two functions.
Multiplicative functions are arithmetical functions that satisfy certain properties, such as being completely multiplicative or strongly multiplicative.
Arithmetical functions have numerous applications in number theory, including the study of prime numbers, modular forms, and elliptic curves.

concepts.name: Arithmetical function
concepts.definition: A function defined on the set of positive integers, assigning real or complex numbers to these integers.

concepts.name: Dirichlet product
concepts.definition: A binary operation on arithmetical functions, used to define the convolution of two functions.

concepts.name: Multiplicative function
concepts.definition: An arithmetical function that satisfies certain properties, such as being completely multiplicative or strongly multiplicative.

claims.text: Matrix groups are groups of matrices with certain properties, such as being invertible or having a specific determinant.
The general linear group GLn(F) is the group of all invertible n x n matrices with entries in a field F.
The special linear group SLn(F) is the subgroup of GLn(F) consisting of all matrices with determinant 1.
Matrix groups have numerous applications in linear algebra, geometry, and physics, including the study of symmetries, transformations, and representations.

concepts.name: Matrix group
concepts.definition: A group of matrices with certain properties, such as being invertible or having a specific determinant.

concepts.name: General linear group
concepts.definition: The group of all invertible n x n matrices with entries in a field F, denoted as GLn(F).

concepts.name: Special linear group
concepts.definition: The subgroup of GLn(F) consisting of all matrices with determinant 1, denoted as SLn(F).

sections.heading: Cosets of Subgroups and Lagrange’s Theorem

claims.text: Given a subgroup H of a group G, a left coset of H is a set of the form gH, where g is an element of G.
Lagrange's theorem states that the order of a subgroup H of a finite group G divides the order of G.
The index of a subgroup H in a group G is the number of left cosets of H in G.
Cosets and Lagrange's theorem have numerous applications in group theory, including the study of subgroups, homomorphisms, and group actions.

concepts.name: Coset
concepts.definition: A set of the form gH, where g is an element of a group G and H is a subgroup of G.

concepts.name: Lagrange's theorem
concepts.definition: A theorem stating that the order of a subgroup H of a finite group G divides the order of G.

concepts.name: Index of a subgroup
concepts.definition: The number of left cosets of a subgroup H in a group G.

claims.text: A normal subgroup N of a group G is a subgroup that is invariant under conjugation by all elements of G.
The factor group G/N is the group of all cosets of N in G, with the operation being defined by (aN)(bN) = (ab)N.
The first isomorphism theorem states that if f is a homomorphism from a group G to a group H, then the image of f is isomorphic to the factor group G/ker(f).
Normal subgroups and factor groups have numerous applications in group theory, including the study of group homomorphisms, quotient groups, and group extensions.

concepts.name: Normal subgroup
concepts.definition: A subgroup that is invariant under conjugation by all elements of a group G.

concepts.name: Factor group
concepts.definition: The group of all cosets of a normal subgroup N in a group G, denoted as G/N.

concepts.name: First isomorphism theorem
concepts.definition: A theorem stating that if f is a homomorphism from a group G to a group H, then the image of f is isomorphic to the factor group G/ker(f).

claims.text: The commutator subgroup G' of a group G is the subgroup generated by all commutators [a, b] = aba^(-1)b^(-1) of elements a and b in G.
The derived series of a group G is the series of subgroups G > G' > G'' >..., where G' is the commutator subgroup of G and G'' is the commutator subgroup of G'.
A maximal subgroup M of a group G is a proper subgroup that is not contained in any other proper subgroup of G.
Special subgroups have numerous applications in group theory, including the study of solvable groups, nilpotent groups, and simple groups.

concepts.name: Commutator subgroup
concepts.definition: The subgroup generated by all commutators [a, b] = aba^(-1)b^(-1) of elements a and b in a group G.

concepts.name: Derived series
concepts.definition: The series of subgroups G > G' > G'' >..., where G' is the commutator subgroup of G and G'' is the commutator subgroup of G'.

concepts.name: Maximal subgroup
concepts.definition: A proper subgroup that is not contained in any other proper subgroup of a group G.

sections.heading: Bijan Davvaz
sections.text: is Professor at the Department of Mathematics, Yazd University, Iran. Earlier, he served as the Head of the Department of Mathematics (1998–2002), Chairman of the Faculty of Science (2004–2006), and Vice-President for Research (2006–2008) at Yazd University, Iran. He earned his Ph.D. in Mathematics with a thesis on “Topics in Algebraic Hyperstructures” from Tarbiat Modarres University, Iran, and completed his M.Sc. in Mathematics from the University of Tehran, Iran. His areas of interest include algebra, algebraic hyperstructures, rough sets and fuzzy logic.Ontheeditorialboardsfor25mathematicaljournals,Prof.Davvazhasauthored 6 books and over 600 research papers, especially on algebra, fuzzy logic, algebraic hyperstructures and their applications. xi

claims.text: Bijan Davvaz is Professor at the Department of Mathematics, Yazd University, Iran.
He earned his Ph.D. in Mathematics with a thesis on “Topics in Algebraic Hyperstructures” from Tarbiat Modarres University, Iran.
His areas of interest include algebra, algebraic hyperstructures, rough sets and fuzzy logic.
Prof. Davvaz has authored 6 books and over 600 research papers, especially on algebra, fuzzy logic, algebraic hyperstructures and their applications.

concepts.name: rough sets
concepts.definition: a mathematical approach to dealing with vagueness and uncertainty in data.

concepts.name: fuzzy logic
concepts.definition: a mathematical approach to dealing with uncertainty and imprecision in data.
